jurisdiction: European Union; reaches providers established outside the EU whose systems are used by persons in the EU
summary: A system intended to interact directly with people must be designed so that those people are aware they are dealing with an AI system rather than a human, unless that is already obvious to a reasonably observant person in the circumstances. The information must reach the person at the point of first interaction.

gate_criteria.criterion: Does this system interact directly with natural persons, and if so, is the disclosure present in the interaction path that will actually be released?
Is the disclosure legible at first interaction rather than reachable only through help text, terms or a settings menu?
Where reliance is placed on the obviousness exception, has that judgement been recorded with reasons?

controls.control: Disclosure rendered in the interface at the opening of every interaction path, including non-default entry points
Accessibility of the disclosure itself — it must survive screen readers, reduced motion and text-only rendering
Release checklist item preventing deployment of a new interaction path without disclosure review
Flow-down of the requirement to any third party embedding or reselling the system
Disclosure rendered in the languages of the affected audience, determined by where the system is made available rather than by the language of development
Translated disclosures reviewed for meaning rather than machine-translated, since a disclosure that is present but not understood does not inform the person

evidence_types.record: Design artefact showing the disclosure in each interaction path, versioned
evidence_types.retention: life of system plus applicable limitation period

evidence_types.record: Release approval recording that disclosure review was completed
Recorded reasons where the obviousness exception was relied on
Periodic rendering check across supported clients and assistive technologies
evidence_types.retention: rolling, minimum one full review cycle

assurance_activities: Independent walkthrough of each interaction path against the recorded design artefact
Sampling of releases to confirm the checklist item was applied and not waived
Review of obviousness-exception decisions for consistency

source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (ELI: https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/1744/oj/eng); European Commission guidelines on the Article 50 transparency obligations, adopted July 2026.
notes: Open-source licensing is not an exemption from Article 50. Note that the duty is on design, so it is discharged before execution — which is why it belongs at the admissibility gate rather than in downstream evidence. Unaffected by the Omnibus amendments: the disclosure duty applies from 2 August 2026 with no transitional period.
